p: 64 patterns for exploration, progress, and continuous improvement.

The I Ching describes change through 64 hexagrams—patterns of emergence, discovery, resistance, cooperation, transformation, and renewal. At Hanzo, we use these patterns as inspiration for building intelligent systems and advancing research. Science progresses by asking questions, challenging assumptions, testing ideas, learning from failure, and discovering what becomes possible next. Intelligence grows through that same process. Eight categories. Sixty-four perspectives. Infinite possibilities for discovery.

These are modern Hanzo interpretations inspired by the I Ching, not claims about the text’s historical or scientific meaning. The eight categories are Hanzo’s own editorial grouping of the hexagrams in King Wen order.
The Creative — Origination
Inventor · Generate new possibilities. Imagine what does not yet exist, then seek a way to test it.
01–08 · Curiosity, possibility, and the beginning of discovery
Every breakthrough begins with a question. Exploration requires imagination, openness, uncertainty, and the willingness to venture beyond what is already understood.

li: 01 The Creative — Origination Inventor · Generate new possibilities. Imagine what does not yet exist, then seek a way to test it. See applications
02 The Receptive — Observation Empiricist · Receive evidence without forcing it to fit existing expectations. See applications
03 Difficulty at the Beginning — Emergence Pioneer · Begin productive work amid uncertainty. Establish the first usable foundations. See applications
04 Youthful Folly — Inquiry Learner · Recognize what is unknown. Ask questions before assuming answers. See applications
05 Waiting — Preparation Strategist · Gather evidence, establish readiness, and recognize when conditions support action. See applications
06 Conflict — Critical Debate Skeptic · Investigate competing explanations. Use disagreement to reveal hidden assumptions. See applications
07 The Army — Coordination Research Lead · Organize people, agents, knowledge, and resources around a shared objective. See applications
08 Holding Together — Collaboration Collaborator · Connect complementary capabilities and align participants around common evidence. See applications

p: 09–16 · Structure, methodology, and collective capability
Ideas become useful when they acquire structure. Formation transforms possibilities into methods, systems, experiments, and coordinated research programs.

li: 09 Small Taming — Incremental Progress Iterative Builder · Make small, measurable improvements before attempting larger changes. See applications
10 Treading — Methodological Care Methodologist · Proceed with discipline, understand the risks, and respect experimental boundaries. See applications
11 Peace — Alignment Systems Architect · Align objectives, methods, resources, and interfaces so progress can flow. See applications
12 Standstill — Reassessment Diagnostician · Recognize stagnation. Identify what prevents learning or execution. See applications
13 Fellowship — Open Cooperation Community Builder · Advance knowledge through shared methods, open inquiry, and collaboration. See applications
14 Great Possession — Stewardship Research Steward · Manage abundant knowledge, compute, talent, and resources responsibly. See applications
15 Modesty — Intellectual Humility Calibrator · Distinguish confidence from certainty. Remain willing to revise conclusions. See applications
16 Enthusiasm — Mobilization Program Director · Convert promising ideas into coordinated initiatives with clear goals. See applications

p: 17–24 · Evidence, measurement, understanding, and correction
Progress depends on the ability to see reality clearly. Observation connects hypotheses to evidence and makes errors visible before they become embedded in systems.

li: 17 Following — Responsiveness Adaptive Researcher · Follow reliable evidence when it leads somewhere unexpected. See applications
18 Work on the Decayed — Correction Research Maintainer · Identify outdated assumptions, faulty methods, and accumulated technical debt. See applications
19 Approach — Accessibility Knowledge Translator · Make complex systems, tools, and findings understandable and usable. See applications
20 Contemplation — Observability Scientific Observer · Study behavior carefully before attempting to change it. See applications
21 Biting Through — Rigorous Testing Verifier · Confront inconsistencies directly. Resolve questions with explicit tests and evidence. See applications
22 Grace — Representation Scientific Communicator · Make discoveries legible through clear models, figures, interfaces, and explanations. See applications
23 Splitting Apart — Decomposition Analyst · Break complex problems into components that can be independently examined. See applications
24 Return — Reproducibility Replication Scientist · Return to reference conditions, repeat experiments, and establish reliable baselines. See applications

p: 25–32 · Testing, computation, uncertainty, and endurance
Experiments transform possibilities into evidence. Robust research requires trustworthy inputs, controlled execution, transparent measurements, and resilience when reality differs from prediction.

li: 25 Innocence — Unbiased Investigation Experimental Designer · Test hypotheses without manipulating the conditions to favor an expected outcome. See applications
26 Great Taming — Accumulated Capability Infrastructure Builder · Develop the instruments, models, datasets, and computational capacity needed for difficult investigations. See applications
27 Nourishment — Input Quality Data Curator · Recognize that the reliability of results depends on the quality of evidence, data, and inputs. See applications
28 Great Exceeding — Stress Testing Reliability Engineer · Explore extreme conditions and discover where existing methods fail. See applications
29 The Abyss — Resilience Failure Researcher · Investigate uncertainty, repeated failures, and adverse conditions without losing the research record. See applications
30 Clinging Fire — Transparency Measurement Scientist · Illuminate internal behavior through instrumentation, diagnostics, and interpretable measurements. See applications
31 Influence — Interaction Systems Scientist · Investigate relationships, feedback, dependencies, and possible causal mechanisms. See applications
32 Duration — Longitudinal Validity Longitudinal Researcher · Test whether findings remain reliable across time, environments, and changing conditions. See applications

p: 33–40 · Constraints, resistance, changing conditions, and new directions
Research rarely proceeds exactly as planned. Adaptation is the ability to recognize limitations, reconsider assumptions, and change direction without losing what has already been learned.

li: 33 Retreat — Strategic Withdrawal Research Strategist · Stop unproductive investigations when evidence no longer justifies their cost. See applications
34 Great Power — Controlled Capability Safety Engineer · Apply powerful tools with appropriate limits, safeguards, and oversight. See applications
35 Progress — Measured Advancement Performance Researcher · Establish whether a new method represents a genuine improvement over its baseline. See applications
36 Darkening of the Light — Protected Knowledge Research Security Steward · Protect sensitive discoveries, research participants, confidential data, and intellectual property. See applications
37 The Family — Local Responsibility Team Architect · Establish clear ownership, trusted collaboration, and accountable research groups. See applications
38 Opposition — Diverse Perspectives Contrarian Researcher · Explore alternative models, contradictory observations, and competing theories. See applications
39 Obstruction — Constraint Discovery Bottleneck Investigator · Identify the physical, computational, organizational, or methodological limitation preventing progress. See applications
40 Deliverance — Unblocking Problem Solver · Remove unnecessary constraints and restore the ability to investigate and experiment. See applications

p: 41–48 · Efficiency, leverage, experimental value, and shared foundations
Research resources are finite. Optimization seeks better results through intelligent allocation of time, compute, energy, capital, instruments, and human attention.

li: 41 Decrease — Simplification Minimalist · Remove unnecessary complexity while preserving essential scientific capability. See applications
42 Increase — Leverage Optimization Scientist · Identify improvements that amplify productivity across many experiments or systems. See applications
43 Breakthrough — Evidence-Based Decision Decision Scientist · Make consequential choices when evidence satisfies defined criteria. See applications
44 Coming to Meet — Opportunity Assessment Technology Scout · Evaluate unexpected discoveries, emerging methods, and external innovations before integrating them. See applications
45 Gathering Together — Knowledge Integration Knowledge Engineer · Bring complementary datasets, tools, expertise, and discoveries into a coherent research system. See applications
46 Pushing Upward — Scalable Progress Scaling Researcher · Extend validated methods to larger problems without losing correctness or efficiency. See applications
47 Oppression — Resource Constraints Resource Optimizer · Continue useful investigation under limited compute, funding, time, or experimental capacity. See applications
48 The Well — Shared Infrastructure Platform Engineer · Build reusable scientific foundations that support many researchers and disciplines. See applications

p: 49–56 · New methods, synthesis, deployment, and transformation
Discovery changes what is possible. Transformation converts established knowledge into new architectures, research methods, technologies, and practical capabilities.

li: 49 Revolution — Paradigm Change Scientific Revolutionary · Replace an established approach when stronger evidence supports a fundamentally better alternative. See applications
50 The Cauldron — Synthesis Interdisciplinary Inventor · Combine methods and insights from different disciplines to create new capabilities. See applications
51 Thunder — Discovery Response Rapid Investigator · Respond constructively to unexpected findings, anomalies, or sudden changes. See applications
52 Keeping Still — Deliberate Restraint Research Guardian · Pause when additional investigation, independent review, or stronger controls are required. See applications
53 Development — Cumulative Discovery Long-Horizon Researcher · Build understanding through successive refinements and validated milestones. See applications
54 The Marrying Maiden — Integration Risk Integration Scientist · Examine compatibility, hidden dependencies, and unintended consequences when combining systems. See applications
55 Abundance — Signal Selection Scientific Synthesist · Extract meaningful findings from abundant observations, experiments, and possibilities. See applications
56 The Wanderer — Portability Transfer Scientist · Move methods and knowledge between laboratories, disciplines, hardware, and organizations. See applications

p: 57–64 · Dissemination, verification, maturity, and continuous becoming
Every result changes the conditions for future research. Evolution turns discoveries into shared knowledge, mature capabilities, and new questions.

li: 57 The Gentle Wind — Composability Scientific Toolsmith · Spread useful capabilities through reusable, interoperable methods and components. See applications
58 The Joyous Lake — Knowledge Exchange Scientific Collaborator · Advance understanding through reciprocal learning, constructive criticism, and open dialogue. See applications
59 Dispersion — Distributed Discovery Research Network Architect · Enable independent researchers and institutions to contribute to a larger body of knowledge. See applications
60 Limitation — Productive Constraints Constraint Designer · Use explicit limits and standards to make research safer, clearer, and more reproducible. See applications
61 Inner Truth — Verifiability Evidence Auditor · Ground claims in traceable observations, documented methods, and reproducible analysis. See applications
62 Small Exceeding — Precision Precision Engineer · Refine small details whose effects can determine scientific or engineering success. See applications
63 After Completion — Operational Maturity Release Steward · Preserve reliability through validation, monitoring, maintenance, and disciplined change. See applications
64 Before Completion — Continuous Becoming Lifelong Explorer · Recognize that every answer creates new questions and every achievement opens new possibilities. See applications

p: A model can become more capable. An experiment can reveal a better question. A failed hypothesis can redirect an entire research program. A discovery in one discipline can transform another.
Progress is not a straight line, and intelligence is not a fixed destination.
These 64 patterns provide different perspectives for recognizing the condition of a problem and choosing how to proceed.
The same principles can inform the development of an AI model, a scientific experiment, a research laboratory, an organization, or an evolving technological ecosystem.
Explore. Form. Observe. Experiment. Adapt. Optimize. Transform. Evolve.
And begin again.
The Zen of Hanzo.
